note: Cerebellar atrophy is variable in TUBA4A-associated spastic ataxia (SPAX11), ranging from normal/slight to overt atrophy across cohorts, making a duration-dependent progression model clinically and biologically plausible.

evidence.text: In patients with the p.Glu415Lys TUBA4A variant, brain MRI revealed slight or absent cerebellar atrophy in several affected individuals.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: MRI showed slight or absent cerebellar atrophy.

evidence.text: Across a cohort of individuals with TUBA4A mutations presenting with ataxia and spasticity, brain imaging demonstrated cerebellar atrophy in 7 out of 11 evaluated patients, confirming variability in cerebellar volume loss.

source.title: De novo and inherited monoallelic variants in TUBA4A cause ataxia and spasticity
source.quote: Brain imaging was performed for 11 cases and showed cerebellar atrophy in seven cases
